definition: The Positive and Negative Affect Schedule is a self-report measure of two separate dimensions of affectivity: positive affect and negative affect. It is used to assess a person’s general tendency toward states such as enthusiasm and alertness on one hand, and distressing emotions such as anxiety, anger, fear, and guilt on the other.

reasons: The packet excerpt states PANAS is designed to measure two distinct temperamental/personality traits (trait positive affect and trait negative affect), and it provides examples of the PA and NA affective states; however, it does not explicitly describe PANAS as a “self-report measure” in the supplied text.
The packet supports PANAS as a measure of trait positive affect and trait negative affect, but it does not explicitly support describing it as a self-report measure.

The definition adds “general tendency” language that is broadly consistent with trait affectivity, but the packet does not state this as a general tendency in those terms; it frames PANAS as measuring trait positive affect and trait negative affect.

The wording “used to assess” and the examples of enthusiastic, alert, anxiety, anger, fear, and guilt are supported, but the full definition combines supported and unsupported claims in a way that is not fully grounded in the packet.
